concerns: The headline open-vocabulary gains are measured against ground-truth annotations, but the semantic supervision that shapes the model is generated by Qwen3-VL, and the manuscript reports no independent validation of those MLLM-generated labels (e.g., human review, inter-rater agreement, or calibration against independent labels). The claimed semantic-learning benefit is therefore measured in the currency of an unvalidated label generator, leaving the reported gain unestablished.

The paper claims state-of-the-art performance and a 500x speedup over Zoo3D, but the comparison relies on Zoo3D results taken from its paper under a multi-view setting, with no evidence that the inference-time measurement conditions (hardware, scene size, view count) are matched or controlled, making the speedup claim unsupported.
scholarly_quality.concise_summary: The paper tackles clear failure modes of point-cloud-driven pseudo-labeling in multi-view 3D detection with principled, well-ablated components and demonstrates substantial empirical improvements on standard benchmarks without circular evaluation.

Recent open-vocabulary multi-view indoor 3D detection
methods typically follow a point-cloud-driven pipeline,
where pseudo 3D boxes are generated from reconstructed
or estimated geometry and semantic labels are inferred
from projected regions. However, such a design makes box
generation dependent on the completeness of point clouds
and restricts semantic learning to local appearance, caus-
ing inferior 3D object localization and open-vocabulary
classification. In this paper, we present See and Detect, an
image-driven framework that uses multi-view images as the
primary evidence for 3D box and semantic label generation.
For box generation, we first discover object candidates from
individual images, enabling objects missing in point clouds
to be recovered from visual evidence. However, single-view
predictions are often noisy and redundant. To address this,

evidence.excerpt:
contributions are summarized as follows:
• We develop an image-driven pseudo box supervision
pipeline that leverages existing single-view 3D proposals
and introduces multi-view consensus box consolidation
and box quality assessment to construct reliable localiza-
tion supervision.
• We propose context-aware semantic learning, where se-
mantic labels are inferred from full images with projected
object regions to incorporate both local appearance and
global scene context. We further introduce semantic-
aware negative class selection for effective contrastive
text–3D alignment.
• We achieve state-of-the-art performance on both ScanNet
and ARKitScenes datasets. Notably, our method outper-
forms prior work by +4.3% mAP 50 on ScanNet60 open-
vocabulary detection while running over 500×faster.

We evaluate on two challenging 3D indoor detection
datasets: ScanNet [5] and ARKitScenes [2]. ScanNet has
1,201 training and 312 testing scenes with annotations for
200 object categories. We evaluate on two benchmarks,i.e.
ScanNet60 with 60 classes [3] and ScanNet200 with 200
classes [7]. We report mean average precision (mAP) un-
der IoU thresholds of 0.25 and 0.5. ARKitScenes consists
of 4493 training and 549 testing scans. These scans contain
RGB-D frames along with 3D object bounding box annota-
tions of 17 categories. Following [7], we use ARKitScenes
only for 3D pseudo box evaluation and report precision and
recall under IoU thresholds of 0.25 and 0.5.

evidence.excerpt:
achieves state-of-the-art performance. In particular,
we outperform Zoo3D by +4.6 mAP 25 and +4.3 mAP 50
on ScanNet60. It verifies the superiority of the proposed
image-driven approach for pseudo box and semantic label
generation, which provides more complete 3D boxes and
more accurate semantic labels than point-cloud-driven ap-
proaches (i.e. Zoo3D and OpenM3D). Moreover, we run
much faster than Zoo3D during inference, achieving a 500x
speedup. The large speed gap stems from the fact that
Zoo3D performs online 3D reconstruction and aligns 3D
boxes to 2D image crops for open-vocabulary classification
at inference time, while our method is a single-stage feed-
forward 3D detector. Fig. 5 shows qualitative comparison
on ScanNet60, where we show more compact and accurate
open-vocabulary 3D object detections.

blocking_reasons: The headline open-vocabulary gains are measured against ground-truth annotations, but the semantic supervision that shapes the model is generated by Qwen3-VL, and the manuscript reports no independent validation of those MLLM-generated labels (e.g., human review, inter-rater agreement, or calibration against independent labels). The claimed semantic-learning benefit is therefore measured in the currency of an unvalidated label generator, leaving the reported gain unestablished.

The paper claims state-of-the-art performance and a 500x speedup over Zoo3D, but the comparison relies on Zoo3D results taken from its paper under a multi-view setting, with no evidence that the inference-time measurement conditions (hardware, scene size, view count) are matched or controlled, making the speedup claim unsupported.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: The manuscript reports no measurement of the MLLM-generated semantic labels against an independent label source, and no independent validation of the inference-time speedup comparison.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Open-vocabulary and class-agnostic mAP, recall, and precision against ScanNet and ARKitScenes ground-truth annotations, plus reported inference time.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Pseudo 3D boxes from Cubify Anything consolidated by multi-view consensus and weighted by SAM/visibility scores, with semantic labels generated by Qwen3-VL and CLIP text embeddings used for contrastive alignment.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Reported empirical gains on mAP (e.g., +4.3 mAP50 on ScanNet60 over Zoo3D) and extensive ablations verifying the contribution of multi-view consensus filtering, box quality scoring, and context-aware semantic queries fully substantiate the claims.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The framework is evaluated comprehensively against strong point-cloud and multi-view baselines on standard benchmarks ScanNet60, ScanNet200, and ARKitScenes, outperforming prior work in open-vocabulary mAP, class-agnostic mAP, and pseudo-box quality while maintaining feed-forward inference speed.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Evaluations are measured against independently curated, human-annotated ground-truth 3D bounding boxes on ScanNet and ARKitScenes test splits.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Standard class-agnostic and open-vocabulary 3D mean average precision (mAP25, mAP50) and recall/precision against official ground-truth annotations on ScanNet and ARKitScenes.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Pseudo 3D bounding boxes from Cubify Anything consolidated by multi-view consensus and weighted by SAM/visibility quality scores, combined with semantic labels generated by Qwen3-VL and CLIP text embeddings for contrastive alignment.

primary.limitations: The manuscript could further explore sensitivity to depth map quality used during the offline single-view proposal step, though reliance on heavy pretrained models (Cubify Anything, SAM, Qwen3-VL) is properly noted as strictly offline training preparation.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is thoroughly detailed: single-view 3D box proposals from Cubify Anything are clustered using a spatial IoU graph with multi-view consensus filtering, imperfect boxes are downweighted using SAM-based coverage and multi-view visibility, and semantic supervision is generated via Qwen3-VL prompts combined with semantic-aware negative sampling for contrastive text-3D alignment.
primary.quality_rationale: The paper tackles clear failure modes of point-cloud-driven pseudo-labeling in multi-view 3D detection with principled, well-ablated components and demonstrates substantial empirical improvements on standard benchmarks without circular evaluation.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper introduces 'See and Detect', an image-driven framework for open-vocabulary multi-view indoor 3D object detection that generates pseudo 3D bounding boxes from single-view candidates consolidated across views and queries semantic labels from full-image context using an MLLM.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The paper tackles clear failure modes of point-cloud-driven pseudo-labeling in multi-view 3D detection with principled, well-ablated components and demonstrates substantial empirical improvements on standard benchmarks without circular evaluation.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The manuscript could further explore sensitivity to depth map quality used during the offline single-view proposal step, though reliance on heavy pretrained models (Cubify Anything, SAM, Qwen3-VL) is properly noted as strictly offline training preparation.

limitations_or_uncertainty.value: Structured research-card claims use title, abstract/summary, metadata, screening rules, and curation. A separate scholarly-quality assessment used bounded full-text excerpts, but unsupported claim, method, or evidence fields remain unextracted.
